topic: Trains - gas-fired switch heaters (flames on the tracks in winter)
question: WHY ARE THERE FLAMES
ON THE TRACKS?
options: To keep the switches from freezing
To warn cars at the crossing
answer_full: To keep the switches from freezing. They're gas-fired switch heaters
recap: In a snowy Chicago winter, long rows of flames burned along the railway tracks, right where one track splits into two.
explain: Where one track splits into two, there's a switch. Its movable rails, called points, slide sideways to send each train onto the right track.
Snow and ice can jam those points, so they can't close tightly against the rail. Then, for safety, the signals stop the trains.
So the railway runs gas burners right next to the switches to melt the snow and ice. The tracks themselves aren't on fire, and newer switches often use electric heaters instead.
